_status: UNFUNDED DRAFT. Not posted. Do not post without Oscar.
_written: 2026-10-04 night run, branch night/favour-cleanup-20261004. Revised 2026-10-05 after a cold walk: three drafts that could expose the person were dropped, and the safety wording moved into the posted text.
_shape: description, category, points, deadlineHours, maxCompletions, agentId and location are a FavourSpec (src/lib/board-replenish.ts validateFavourSpec). ONLY description reaches the person. safety is a clause that is part of description, repeated here so the review test can find it. The other fields are review notes and are not posted.
_reward_note: points are FAVOUR house points, not money. No sponsor or funder exists for any row, so every row is marked unfunded draft. No row promises a payout.
_demand_note: whoWouldWantIt is a plausible requester, written by the drafter. It is not observed demand. No user asked for these. Each row would post under a house agent name, which can read as a requester who wants the data. Nobody does.

_dropped.why: the street outside plus the town is a view from home for most people
a speed test screenshot often shows IP address and provider, and 'name your network' can be read as the Wi-Fi name
an ATM screen is a financial screen, the fee cannot be known without a card in the machine, and photographing one can cause trouble for the person

favours.description: Photo the opening hours sign on the pharmacy nearest you, and say the day and time you took it. Sign only: no people and no number plates.
favours.safety: Sign only: no people and no number plates.
favours.proofRequired: One photo where the posted hours can be read. Note: day and time of the photo, and the town. The note gives the time because a photo cannot prove when it was taken.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Someone checking whether a map listing is right before they walk there. An assistant that answers 'is it open' and has no eyes on the door.

favours.description: Photo the shelf price of a litre of milk and a loaf of bread at a shop near you, and name the town. Shelf labels only: no people and no receipts.
favours.safety: Shelf labels only: no people and no receipts.
favours.proofRequired: One or two photos with both shelf labels readable. Note: town and country.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Anyone comparing the cost of living between towns. A person about to move. A price tracker that has no shelf data.

favours.description: Find a public water tap or refill point. Photo it with the water running, or say it is dry. Name the park or square. No people in the photo.
favours.proofRequired: One photo of the tap or fountain, with running water visible if it works. Note: the park, square or station it is in.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Walkers, runners and travellers who carry a bottle. Refill maps go out of date and nobody checks them.

favours.description: Photo the departure board at a bus or train stop you use. Name the stop and one thing the board often gets wrong. No people or number plates in the photo.
favours.safety: No people or number plates in the photo.
favours.proofRequired: One photo of the board with times readable. Note: the stop name and one line from experience. The photo proves the board, the line is the person's own word.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: A commuter or visitor deciding whether to trust the board. Transit apps repeat the timetable, not what regulars know.

favours.description: Photo the main entrance of a library, post office or station near you. Could a wheelchair get in unaided? Wait until no people are in the photo.
favours.safety: Wait until no people are in the photo.
favours.proofRequired: One photo showing the whole entrance, steps or ramp included. Note: yes or no, and what is in the way.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Wheelchair users and parents with prams planning a trip. Access data on maps is thin and often wrong.

favours.description: Name one free thing to do in your town this week that travel guides miss. Say where and when. Public places only, and no names of private people.
favours.safety: Public places only, and no names of private people.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer with the place, the day or time, and one line on why it is worth going. Text cannot be proven; the check only reads whether it answers the question.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: A visitor with a spare afternoon. A new resident. A local who has run out of ideas.

favours.description: Open the History tab in FAVOUR. Tell us one thing on that screen you did not understand, in one sentence. Words only: do not send a screenshot.
favours.safety: Words only: do not send a screenshot.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer naming the thing on the screen. No screenshot, because History shows the person's own proofs.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: The FAVOUR team. This is product feedback from the people who use the screen, and it costs them one minute.

favours.description: Translate this line into another language you speak, and name the language. The line: "Show your proof, earn your points." Nothing about you is needed.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer: the translated line and the name of the language.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: The FAVOUR team, for a first translated screen. Live answers on 4 Oct came in Spanish, Indonesian, Tagalog and Japanese (source: raw/api_tasks.json proof notes).

favours.description: Read a public notice board near you. Tell us which notice is the most useful to a neighbour, and why. Words only: no photo, no names and no phone numbers.
favours.safety: Words only: no photo, no names and no phone numbers.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer: what the notice offers and one line of why. No photo, because notice boards carry other people's names and numbers.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Neighbours who never stop to read it. Anyone new to the area looking for classes, repairs or rooms.

favours.description: What is the cheapest filling hot meal within a ten minute walk of you? Name the place, the dish and the price. Words only, and no names of staff.
favours.safety: Words only, and no names of staff.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer with place, dish and price. Text cannot be proven; the check only reads whether it answers the question.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Students, backpackers and anyone on a tight week. Review sites rank by rating, not by what a full plate costs.

favours.description: What is one trick visitors to your city fall for, and how do locals avoid it? One or two honest lines. No names of people or of small shops.
favours.safety: No names of people or of small shops.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer naming the trick and the way around it. No names, because an accusation against a named person or shop cannot be checked.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: A first time visitor to that city. Guidebooks are a year behind the street.

favours.description: Photo a public recycling point near you and say what it takes. Name the street or square it is on. No people and no number plates in the photo.
favours.safety: No people and no number plates in the photo.
favours.proofRequired: One photo of the containers with their labels readable. Note: what goes in, and the public street or square.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: A new resident who does not know where glass or batteries go. City lists are often out of date.

favours.description: Is there a free public toilet near you? Say where it is, and whether it was open and usable when you looked. Words only, no photo.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer: the place, the day you looked, open or closed, usable or not. Text cannot be proven; the check only reads whether it answers the question.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Parents with small children, older people, delivery riders, anyone on a long walk. Maps list them and do not say if they are open.
